content: Interventions for treating injuries to the medial ligaments of the knee involve various approaches depending on the severity and type of injury. These may include conservative management such as rest, ice application, compression, and elevation (RICE), alongside physical therapy to restore strength and range of motion. In cases of partial tears, bracing or immobilization may be recommended to allow the ligament to heal properly. For complete tears or injuries associated with other structural damage in the knee, surgical repair or reconstruction may be necessary. Post-treatment rehabilitation is critical to ensure optimal recovery and to minimize the risk of long-term complications such as instability or chronic pain.
